items.heading: Replacing a blown light bulb
precautionsFirst: Switch off the light switch and let the bulb cool completely before touching it.
Do not touch a bulb, socket, or switch with wet hands.
Use a stable stool or ladder on solid ground rather than standing on furniture.
details: Turn off the switch and, if possible, the circuit breaker for that light.
Once the old bulb has cooled, turn it counter-clockwise (screw type) or press and twist (bayonet type) to remove it.
Check that the new bulb's wattage and base type match the fitting.
Insert the new bulb and turn clockwise, or press and twist, until snug - do not overtighten.
Switch the power back on and test.

items.heading: Resetting a tripped MCB or circuit breaker
precautionsFirst: Do not reset the breaker repeatedly if it trips again immediately - that signals a fault needing an electrician.
Keep hands dry and stand on a dry surface while working at the board.
Switch off or unplug high-load appliances on that circuit before resetting.
details: Locate the main distribution board and find the breaker that has flipped to the off or middle position.
Switch off or unplug appliances that may have overloaded that circuit.
Push the breaker firmly to the full off position first, then switch it back on.
If it trips again immediately, do not force it further - call a qualified electrician, as this can indicate a short circuit or wiring fault.

items.heading: Replacing a fuse wire (older fuse boxes)
precautionsFirst: Always switch off the main power supply before touching the fuse box.
Use the correct fuse wire rating for the circuit - never substitute thicker wire, as it removes the safety protection.
If unsure of the correct rating, call an electrician rather than guessing.
details: Turn off the main switch at the distribution board.
Open the fuse carrier for the affected circuit and remove the old, burnt fuse wire.
Fit a new fuse wire of the correct rated capacity across the terminals and tighten the screws.
Close the carrier, restore the main switch, and test the circuit.

items.heading: Fixing a loose or wobbly switch or socket
precautionsFirst: Always switch off the circuit breaker for that point before opening it, not just the switch itself.
Never touch internal wiring while the power is still connected.
If wires look burnt or discolored, or the socket feels warm even when off, stop and call an electrician.
details: Turn off the breaker for that circuit and confirm with a voltage tester, or by checking the switch no longer works.
Unscrew the switch or socket plate carefully and pull it out gently.
Check that the internal wire terminals are tight, and tighten any loose screws with a screwdriver.
Screw the plate back in place, restore power, and test.

items.heading: Fixing a flickering light
precautionsFirst: Turn off power at the breaker before checking the bulb or fitting.
If flickering affects several lights across the house, stop and call an electrician rather than continuing on your own.
details: Turn off the light and check the bulb is screwed in firmly - a loose bulb often flickers.
Try a new bulb, since an old bulb nearing the end of its life is a common cause.
Check whether the fixture uses a dimmer that may be incompatible with the bulb type.
If flickering continues, the issue may be in the wiring or switch itself - call an electrician.

items.heading: Replacing a plug top on a cord
precautionsFirst: Always work with the appliance unplugged and switched off.
Match wire colors to the correct terminals carefully (in India: brown/red = live, blue/black = neutral, green or green-yellow = earth).
Use a plug rated for the appliance's power draw.
details: Unscrew and open the plug casing.
Strip a small length of insulation from each wire if needed, without cutting the copper strands.
Connect the live, neutral, and earth wires to their correctly marked terminals, tightening each screw firmly.
Ensure the cord is gripped securely by the cord clamp inside the plug before closing the casing.
Test the plug in a socket before using it with the appliance.

items.heading: Extension board or power strip not working
precautionsFirst: Unplug the extension board before inspecting it.
Do not overload an extension board beyond its rated capacity.
If it smells burnt or looks melted, discard it rather than trying to repair it.
details: Check the board is plugged in firmly and its switch, if it has one, is on.
Test the wall socket with another device to rule out a socket issue.
Check the fuse inside the extension board's plug, if it has one, and replace it if blown.
If it still does not work and shows no visible damage, replace the extension board rather than opening it.
